title: Introduce cross-account route ownership and DNS handoff for private control plane
author: Asha Nambiar
release_notes: Adds cross-account route ownership tagging and an idempotent DNS handoff worker using Route53 Resolver endpoints; migration step required for existing stacks: run `rwictl migrate-route-ownership`
description:
Summary: Implements a cross-account route ownership model for private control plane VPCs and an automated DNS handoff path that propagates service-records to authorized consumer accounts. Motivations: customers deploying Redwood Private across multiple AWS accounts were manually synchronizing route table updates and forwarding DNS records; this caused operational toil during upgrades and periodic incidents where the control plane lost egress visibility. This PR automates assignment of route ownership via tags, introduces a cross-account role assumption flow, and wires a new 'dns-handoff' Terraform module and a lightweight reconciliation Lambda to propagate Route53 Resolver rules and service-records.

What it does (high level):
- Terraform: new module modules/vpc/route_ownership that tags route tables and creates an IAM role and policy for named-account takeover.
- Terraform: new module modules/dns/dns_handoff that creates Route53 Resolver endpoints, resolver rules with target IPs for consumer accounts, and SSM parameters to share metadata.
- Installer orchestration: the private-installer boot sequence now calls the handoff job as part of the post-controlplane step when `enable_cross_account_handoff=true`.
- Reconciliation: added a small Lambda (go) that runs under a cross-account role to synchronize service A records and conditional forwarder rules; runs as AWS EventBridge scheduled job and on-demand via the installer.
- Backwards compatibility: feature guarded; existing deployments opt-in. Migration helper `rwictl migrate-route-ownership` maps legacy route tags and performs a dry-run before committing.

Checklist: [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested with terratest harness; [x] Installer hook and CLI migration command; [x] IAM least-privilege review completed; [x] E2E smoke test against a 2-account sandbox; [x] Docs and upgrade notes added to private-installer/README.md.

review_thread: Diego Cortez: Left a detailed security-first review asking to narrow the IAM role to specific sts:AssumeRole principals and require external ID; requested unit tests for edge cases where resolver endpoints are in different subnets.
Asha Nambiar: Addressed: tightened role trust policy, added external ID flow, split resolver endpoint creation across AZs and added terratest scenarios for subnet mismatch (see commit 4d5e6f7).

Lina Patel: Asked for clearer observability - requested CloudWatch metrics for handoff successes/failures and trace logs. Also asked whether the reconciliation run can be rate-limited to avoid API throttling during large fleet rollouts.
Asha Nambiar: Added CloudWatch custom metrics and an exponential backoff + jitter to the reconciler; documented rate-limit knobs in modules/dns/dns_handoff/README.md.
Marcus Lee: Manual security approve after validating least-privilege changes; ran a penetration checklist against the lambda and IAM roles and confirmed no over-permissive policies remain.
Diego Cortez: CI flake on aws-integration terratest — re-ran CI and green; approved and performed squash merge.
